display_name: The whole Building (Strata Management) Act 2004 under one top-level goal — is the matter validly decided, may this person sit on the council, and what does a proprietor in arrears face — and six goals: resolutions and meetings, the owner developer, the management corporation, the council, Strata Titles Boards, offences and service
scope: Every provision of the Act as printed in SSO's informal consolidation of the version in force from 1 October 2026 (2020 Revised Edition). Inputs: the Commissioner's, Minister's, Board's and court's discretions and findings; prescribed matters; valid-vote counts; public holidays. Carried as text: the provisions listed in each module and the Fourth Schedule. NOT encoded: nothing in the Act.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the Act. An independent test pass was run on 2026-10-10 (tests-independent.l4, 288 assertions from expectations written before the encoding was read): 286 pass; the 2 failures (E132, E137) are one-day-early expectations the report itself concedes, kept as expected failures. One gap (renewal options in exclusive-use and lease terms) was fixed. The source is SSO's unofficial consolidation. The pipeline has not been run.

forks.F1: s 49(3): the defence is (c) and either (d) or (e).
forks.F2: First Schedule para 1A(6) short notice does not shorten s 2's 15/22 days.
forks.F3: s 40(10): payment on the 14th day after the demand is late.
forks.F4: ss 40(6), 43: 30 days end at the close of day 30.

forks.F6: First Schedule para 9(4): fractions rounded down.
forks.F7: s 101(6): Boards may order only on powers needing no more than an ordinary resolution.
